# Arithmetic builtins: + - * / % pow.

=== add
(+ 1 2)
--- want
3

=== add variadic
(+ 1 2 3 4)
--- want
10

=== add one
(+ 1)
--- want
1

=== add zero args is identity
(+)
--- want
0

=== add floats
(+ 0.1 0.2)
--- want
0.30000000000000004

=== sub
(- 10 3)
--- want
7

=== sub variadic
(- 10 3 2)
--- want
5

=== sub unary negates
(- 5)
--- want
-5

=== sub needs an argument
(-)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== mul
(* 2 3)
--- want
6

=== mul variadic
(* 2 3 4)
--- want
24

=== mul zero args is identity
(*)
--- want
1

=== div
(/ 10 2)
--- want
5

=== div variadic
(/ 100 5 2)
--- want
10

=== div float result
(/ 1 4)
--- want
0.25

=== div by zero
(/ 1 0)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== div zero by zero
(/ 0 0)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== div by float zero
(/ 1 0.0)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== div needs an argument
(/)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== mod
(% 10 3)
--- want
1

=== mod is floored: negative divisor
(% 5 -3)
--- want
-1

=== mod is floored: negative dividend
(% -1 2)
--- want
1

=== mod exact
(% 7 7)
--- want
0

=== mod floats
(% 5.5 2)
--- want
1.5

=== mod negative float dividend
(% -5.5 2)
--- want
0.5

=== mod by zero
(% 1 0)
--- error
--- at 1:1

# The operands below are built from powers of two, which every runtime and
# host computes exactly: a literal like 1e300 is outside what a host without
# a C library promises to read to the last bit, and the case would be about
# number text instead of modulo.

=== mod is exact however large the quotient
(% (pow 2 1000) 7)
--- want
2

=== mod of a huge negative dividend is floored
(% (- (pow 2 1000)) 7)
--- want
5

=== mod by a tiny divisor
(% 7 (* 3 (pow 2 -1000)))
--- want
(pow 2 -1000)

=== mod by infinity gives the dividend back
(% 5 (pow 2 2000))
--- want
5

=== mod by infinity is floored like any other
(% -5 (pow 2 2000))
--- want
(pow 2 2000)

=== mod of infinity is NaN
(% (pow 2 2000) 3)
--- want
(- (pow 2 2000) (pow 2 2000))

=== pow
(pow 2 10)
--- want
1024

=== pow fractional
needs host-pow
(pow 2 0.5)
--- want
1.4142135623730951

# IEEE behavior on every host; Filo does not invent a real cube root.
=== pow of a negative base to a fractional exponent is NaN
(pow -8 (/ 1 3))
--- want
(number "nan")

=== pow zero zero
(pow 0 0)
--- want
1

=== pow arity
(pow 2)
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== type error
(+ 1 "a")
--- error
--- at 1:1

=== type error nested
(* 2 (+ 1 #t))
--- error
--- at 1:6

=== nested arithmetic
(+ (* 2 3) (- 10 4) (/ 8 2))
--- want
16

=== large integers stay exact
(+ 9007199254740992 1)
--- want
9007199254740992

=== unary division is the reciprocal
(/ 4)
--- want
0.25

=== unary division of one
(/ 1)
--- want
1

=== unary division of zero
(/ 0)
--- error
--- at 1:1
